5. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has taken us though the judgments of the Courts below, the plaint and the relevant papers on record and submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in making out a third case that the suit land can-not be definitely ascertained without relayment with the land of patta dated 17th Aswin, 1281 B.S. in order to see as to whether the land was identical or not inasmuch as in view of the rent receipt Ext. E series lead to a presumption of possession in favour of the defendant the findings of the lower appellate Court regarding possession of the plaintiff was contrary to the evidence on record. The learned Advocate further submits that the finding as to the possession of the final Court of fact has been disturbed by the High Court Division on misappreciation of the evidence on record inasmuch as the D. Ws. have themselves supported the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and as such the finding of the High Court Division is not only contrary to the material evidence on record but without any basis whatsoever. 

 14. The plaintiff as well filed Exts. 2 and 3 as to payment of rent on the basis of patta dated 7th Aswin 1381 B.S. and the defendant No. 6 as well filed rent receipt Ext. E series to support their payment of rent in respect of the suit land of S.A. Khatian No. 311. In the case of Lal Meah being dead his heirs Momena Khaton and ors. Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and ors. 28 DLR (AD) 61 it has been held that record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title of land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself, it is not an evidence of title. The presumption of correctness as available to the C.S. record of right in the name of Nazimuddin's  1/3rd share on the strength of Section 1038(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act has been rebutted as the defendants could not show any basis of record in view of patta Ext. 1 in favour of Tajumuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs. Consequently there are also no basis of recording in R.S. and S.A. in the arnes of the recordees other than the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 6 also could not pro-duce any patta or rent receipt in support of the lease in favour of Rahimjan and as such the rent receipts Ext. D series could not confer any title on the defendant No. 6. The plaintiff led evidence of possession and the same has also been supported by D.Ws. Thus the presumption attached to C.S. has been rebutted and as such sub-sequent recording in R.S. and S.A. are of no legal consequence. The khatian being at best evidence of present possession could not be a document of title so as to confer right, title, and interest of the suit land. The defendant having failed to prove any basis of their title by any cogent material, the rent receipt Ext. E series are of no avail to them. When evidence was led in rebuttal of the presumption of correctness of entry in the record of right and the appellate Court below comes to a finding rebutting the presumption, the said finding being finding of fact, arrived at by the final Court of fact on consideration of the evidence on record, is not liable to be interfered with in revision as there was no error of law resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Court of appeal below has considered that no question of any partition in the suit is necessary, as the plaintiff has claimed the entire suit land and mores°, the suit was for declaration of title.
